transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get our pre-run meeting started for the weekend shift on Line 6. We're planning to package 900 finished cartons, and we'd like to use the newly installed robotic palletizer if we can get the right sign-offs. Before I can authorize the run, I need to hear from both the maintenance lead and the quality engineer on their findings. Who'd like to go first?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a serious issue. During my commissioning check of the robotic palletizer, I found that the safety interlock is not holding reliably. Per maintenance policy, that prohibits us from using the robot for this weekend's run. I haven't entered the finding in the maintenance work order yet because the commissioning packet is still awaiting my supervisor's signature, but the issue is real and I can't sign off on the robot. The good news is we can prepare the manual palletizing station in exactly 45 minutes with two trained operators, so we still have a viable path forward for the 900 cartons.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share an important quality requirement. I confirmed in the customer's pilot-packaging instruction that all 900 cartons must receive a barcode scan and be palletized into exactly three family groups: 300 cartons of Family X, 280 cartons of Family Y, and 320 cartons of Family Z. I haven't uploaded the instruction to the quality system yet because the customer service team is still linking the purchase-order revision, but this requirement stands.
transcript.speaker: A3
